scope: Retrospective human-label-budget learning curve specified after the full nested benchmark; not preregistered, independent or prospective evidence.
subset_rule: Sort outer-training compound IDs; permute once with SeedSequence([subsample_seed, outer_fold, split_seed]); finite budgets take nested prefixes. Retain every condition of selected compounds.
paired_budget: Each arm receives exactly the same human training labels, compounds, conditions, gene axis, inner folds and alpha grid. Rat training labels use the same selected pairs; measured test rat responses are available only to the source arm.
kernel: Descriptor NaNs use training-column medians (all-missing training columns use zero); descriptors/context then training z-scores. Kmol=.5 Tanimoto(PubChem881)+.5 RBF(descriptors); Kctx=RBF(context); RBF=exp(-squared distance/(2*dimension)). Kprior=(Kmol+Kctx+Kmol*Kctx)/3, with a fixed molecule-context interaction. Kprior and count-normalized train-z-scored rat linear Ks are separately training-centered and divided by training mean diagonal. Chemical-only prior uses Kprior; source+same-prior=.5 Kprior+.5 Ks. All weights/bandwidth rules fixed before outer evaluation.

molecular_features.join: Case-fold, underscores to spaces, whitespace collapse; no chemical alias inference.
molecular_features.selection_basis: Verified reagent identity and feature availability only; no response values.

data_warnings: Condition-level replicate means do not retain single-cell distributions or replicate variance (Zenodo 20204514).
Historical RMA jointly normalized all available arrays per species before splitting; this pilot remains exploratory and retrospective (source 41a_rma_brainarray.R).
Historical test outcomes have been examined in prior repository analyses; diagnostic_test is not a prospective or untouched test set (artifacts/tg_gates_rat_human_v1/report.md).
Before absolute-concentration filtering: Dose units are missing for retained conditions; equal dose labels or numeric values do not establish concentration matching.
Before absolute-concentration filtering: Nominal concentration comparison is unknown for 100 retained conditions; unsupported units are not concentration matched.
Absolute-concentration retained cohort has zero unknown/ambiguous units; both arms receive planned nominal molar concentrations.
aggregation: Score each seed's OOF predictions separately; average the three seed-specific losses for each compound, then compounds equally. Do not ensemble predictions before loss. All-budget reuse is counted once.
reporting: All planned budgets and seeds are reported. Outer outcomes select no budget, seed, or fallback. Seed variation describes training-composition sensitivity.
limitations: Budgets count historical paired compounds and actual condition rows, without measuring cost, acquisition feasibility or guaranteed reduction of future experiments.
Three subsamples overlap, and models share outer folds; they are not independent replication.
A smaller-budget source model matching a larger-budget prior at a point estimate would not establish economic savings or statistical equivalence.
The same historical normalization, one-species/liver-system and condition-mean limitations apply.

absolute_concentrations.rule: Both planned treatment doses must be finite and positive with uniquely resolved attributes/metadata units among M,mM,uM,μM,nM. Case-sensitive fixed conversion to M followed by log10; no inferred units, mass-to-molar conversion, aliases, or rounding.
absolute_concentrations.information_available_to_both_arms: Time, planned rat concentration, planned human concentration, nominal dose indicators and molecular features. Source-plus-prior alone additionally receives measured rat expression response.
absolute_concentrations.interpretation: Nominal administered molar concentrations; intracellular exposure equivalence is not established. Different verified source/target concentrations are retained.

aggregate.inference_scope: Descriptive compound bootstrap of mean seed-specific losses from fixed OOF predictions. Seeds and fold-trained models share data; no refitting or population-coverage guarantee. Three subsamples do not form independent biological replications.
